utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. The flag is black with this same emblem in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next emblem. What is -- can you say what we see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: This is the emblem of the Serbian Radical Party. For a while it was with a crown. Later on the crown was removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we better have a separate tab number. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now a -- another exhibit. It's actually a map indicating in red dots the places that the witness will now speak about. And it's just as an assistance to everyone to find the location easily without having to find it in an atlas. Witness, there's no need to explain this map now. You just have it there at your convenience. Thank you. And we would need to have a tab number from the Croatian map binder, and it is the Exhibit 326, and it would be tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can I continue? Yes? Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did Seselj hold a rally in Subotica in late 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything related to non-Serbs at this rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. Seselj held a rally in the centre of Subotica, in the square, when he declared that he would take out eyes with rusted forks and spoons of non-Serbs, the Croats and Hungarians living in Subotica that were not loyal to the current authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I may have misled you with my question. Do you recall when that was, in which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I made a mistake in my question. Sorry. Did he make any suggestion of what to do against the non-Serbs in the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. He said that they -- all Croats should be chased out to Croatia, whereas the Serbs who had fled from Croatia should come to their homes. And the same applied to the Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this rally, did he also speak about state borders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, he did. The borders that we saw mentioned in the statute of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik movement. Those are the borders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a name that Seselj used for this Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Greater Serbia with its borders from Karlovac to Karlobag and Virovitica as far as Croatia is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would need now to go into private session, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, before that could we get the year? In 1991. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did such a campaign that was suggested take place in Subotica and the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, it did take place. There were two terrorist attacks. The cathedral, the Catholic church in Subotica, was blown up, and also a plaque with the name of Dusan Stipanovic, a Hungarian name given to a school. That plaque was removed also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were non-Serbs thrown out -- dismissed from the police or other government offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, from the police, the police became Serbian police. Serb refugees were hired. And I was told by the volunteers that I had rallied that I should select capable people to become active members of the police force and members of the reserve force. This same applied to personnel of hospitals and other institutions. There were dismissals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Croats and Hungarians, were they intimidated in their houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Many families moved out of Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the police prevent any of these occurrences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: No, it didn't prevent them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did policemen actually engage in such activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. They engaged in terror, in physical harassment of citizens of Croat and Hungarian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a local SPS structure in Subotica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, in Subotica there was an SPS. The president was Dusko Stipanovic of that branch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this SPS structure involved in the campaign against the non-Serbs or was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: In the same way as the radicals. The Presidency of the Serbian Radical Party and the Presidency of the Serbian Radical Party collaborated on a daily basis, first through dismissals. That was the beginning. Then there were the groups that I mentioned who put explosives in the church, who harassed citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they collaborated on a daily basis. Where were the offices of both those parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The offices were at the Workers' University in Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the perpetrators investigated, disciplined, prosecuted, or convicted to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: No, they weren't, though the perpetrators were known, at least of these bomb attacks. He was temporarily in hospital, but there were no reprisals against them. And the judge in the Subotica district court, Raseta, I don't know his first name, and Mile Kosanovic, one belonged to the Serbian Radical Party and the other to the SPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that non-Serbs fled the region after these occurrences. Do you -- can you give us an estimate on how many people -- non-Serbs fled or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: As far as I know, from the territory of Vojvodina, about 20.000 Hungarians and a large number of Croats were expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know this figure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I know from the SUP, there the documents, from the bulletin we received every morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go into private session just briefly for two questions to get into the next subject.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was a military shooting range, military -- a JNA facility or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: It was a JNA facility, a shooting range, yes, where the troops are trained in the use of firearms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that -- you said that you saw Seselj there and Ostojic and Mihalj Kertes. How did you know -- did you know Mihalj Kertes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I knew Mihalj Kertes also from the media. In those days he was Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing at this military facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: When I was approaching that facility, I saw a lot of people there. I spoke to them. They were people from Ilok, a place in Croatia. And they were distributing firearms, automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I'm referring to Vojislav Seselj, Mihalj Kertes, Jovo Ostojic was there, JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the people from Ilok that received firearms. What kind of people? What ethnic background did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned JNA officers being there. Did they distribute the arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. They were present there next to the boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any senior police officers there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Not over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the scale on which this distribution happened? Just a rough estimate of how many people received arms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I would say about 150 to 200 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will now move on to the Serbian Chetnik movement, and we briefly need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were -- how many volunteers were actually recruited? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, about 300 volunteers were registered in Subotica. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the -- you said that the JNA and the police members were a prime target for this recruitment. What -- did they actu ally join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: There were very many members the Serb Chetnik movement from the ranks of the police and the army, both commissioned and non-commissioned officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did at the same time the SPS recruit volunteers? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that. I saw Dusko Stipanovic recruiting volunteers from the SPS. And he took them to the Dubrovnik frontline, to Krajina, to Lika. They went through the army, through the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- when the Chetnik volunteers were recruited, what was -- what were they told? What were they supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, the task was the struggle against communism. That was the basic objective of that unit in Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other Chetnik units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The other Chetnik units were -- operated more in the zone of war operations, that is to say in Croatia. They fought against the Croats along with the Yugoslav army together with other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war in Croatia ended, what was the purpose of the units then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The units from the Northern Backa district were still intended to fight against communism until 1993. And are you now referring to the beginning of the war in Bosnia? There were other Chetnik units that were transferred to Bosnia then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand at first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. At that time when the Chetniks were recruited for, let's say, Bosnia -- sorry, for Croatia in the beginning, what did you and those people who volunteered knew of what was going on in Croatia? What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, as I said, most of my knowledge came from the media, TV, radio, newspapers. For the most part that the Serb population was jeopardised to a maximum, that they were being massacred, that crimes were being committed against them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently find out whether these reports were correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the war operations zones and I saw that for the most part this was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did happen? What was the truth that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, I saw -- let me put it briefly -- that our army was the aggressor in the territory of the Republic of Croatia. That is to say, they were committing killings, the destruction of houses. They were taking possession of territories, villages, towns. Territories were being ethnically cleansed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also go to Bosnia? And what did you see happening there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to Bosnia. I saw the same thing there where I was, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to the details where exactly you were, but let me ask you one thing. The volunteers that joined the SP movement and the volunteer units, what -- were files kept on them, and if so, who would do that and where were they kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. Records were made when people joined the Serb Chetnik movement first. The volunteer would bring in his military booklet along with his military assignment, that is to say, what he had been trained for. And then he went to the offices of the Serb Chetnik movement. And then in the field, in the zone of war operations, they belonged to the Territorial Defence and to the JNA command. Again records were kept on these men, the number of personnel engaged, names and surnames, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would keep these records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, in Subotica, at the offices of the Serb Chetnik movement, I was the one who kept this. In Belgrade it was Vojislav Seselj and Zoran Drazilovic that kept the archives and in the field where the war operations were, the commands of the TO and of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the volunteers trained in Subotica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: In the area of Subotica, volunteers were trained at the military training grounds and also at the police training grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave the permission for these trainings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The top people of the SUP, Milan Jerinkic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the JNA facility where they trained, who gave the permission and who did the training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Permission was given by Colonel Jovanovic, an officer of the 1st barracks in Subotica. He was the one who gave permission for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the JNA in Subotica also provide weapons or uniforms to the volunteers during the training and in case they went to the frontline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: During training uniforms were not handed out, but it was at the military exercise and training grounds that people were trained to use weapons. So that is where there was a shooting range and where they actually were engaged in shooting. At other locations they actually did give uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the volunteers went to the frontline, how did they receive a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, it depended on where people were going. For the most part they went to Bubanj Potok. This is a military facility near Belgrade. That is where they were issued with complete uniforms, that is to say, clothing and footwear and also training in the use of firearms was conducted there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- Bubanj Potok is near Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did volunteer units also go directly from Subotica to Croatia to combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. People were mostly transferred to Belgrade first. Bubanj Potok, those were not trained to shoot, then they would trained there and then they were issued equipment. And there were also cases when people went directly from Subotica to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they did the latter, that is directly to the front line, where would they get their uniforms and their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Weapons and equipment, they would get it at the command where they would report, the command of the TO and the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the field where they would join combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, in the field, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the uniforms, what kind of uniforms were they, JNA uniforms or different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Those were camouflage uniforms of the army of Yugoslavia, of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have seen insignias from -- you have explained insignias. Did these -- did the volunteers put their Chetnik insignia on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that cause any problems on the front lines? I mean with the JNA officers or the TO officers that received them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: No. There were absolutely no problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did -- how did the -- the structure in Subotica get aware of the need for volunteers? Did you explain how it came about that volunteers ended up, for instance, in Croatia? Can you just explain the way how it went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The Main Staff was in the office in Belgrade of the Serb Radical Party. They would inform the office of the Serb Radical Party in Subotica, and they would inform the officers of the Serb Chetnik movement, and that is how preparations would be carried out to have people sent to the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The initial request for volunteers, would it come from the regions where the combat took place, and who actually would put such a request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. Requests mostly came from the field, from the zone of war operations to the office of the Serb Radical Party, and then they would send it to the local committees in the various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the local command get detailed information to which part of the front the volunteers had to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would be the information that you got, you, the people in the command in Subotica as an example? What information exactly would they get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, for example, that an area, a town was jeopardised by Croats or Muslims in Bosnia and that it was necessary to send assistance and manpower from our side and then food, medicine, footwear, clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how would the volunteers then get to these places where they were needed? How would they be transported?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: We had sponsors, companies, firms that gave us buses free of charge to Belgrade or to the war operations zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "companies," does that include public companies? State-owned organisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would these buses be accompanied -- escorted by any authorities such as police or army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. We would have an escort, military buses escorted by the police or civilian buses escorted by the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived -- when these units arrived in the place where they were supposed to go, to whom would they report and from whom would they get their orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: They would report to the command, the army command in that territory. For example, the Novi Sad Corps, the Kragujevac Corps and also in Bosnia, the command in the field, to the officers of that command where they would arrive.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to go briefly into private session for one matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, before I continue, Mr. Nice has asked me to raise a very brief matter in relation to the previous witness. He actually -- he said that the transcript will only be available tomorrow, and he asked for permission to show the two videos to the previous witness if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you went to Vukovar. My question is, was that before or after it fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Before the fall of Vukovar. I mean, I'm sorry, after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time later? Was it in 1991, in November or December? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Right after the fall. That is to say a few days after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned the Leva Supoderica detachment, and in this context you also mentioned a person, Kameni. This detachment, was that a Serbian volunteer detachment? And Kameni, who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. This was a Chetnik volunteer unit. Milan Lancuzanin, nicknamed Kameni in 1992 was proclaimed a Chetnik vojvoda. He was commander of that detachment, Leva Supoderica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this detachment Leva Supoderica, I would like to show you now tab 9 of your exhibit binder. And it's also in Sanction. And it's an address of the chief, Ljubisa Petkovic of the Serbian Radical Party War Staff of 9th of November, 1991 to that same detachment, and it says here in the first line: "All the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party has sent you, are being placed under your command and the protection of the Vukovar TO. The SRS War Staff has appointed Slobodan Katic, a brave and experienced soldier from Belgrade as the commander of the volunteers in Vukovar." Do you know this person Slobodan Katic and was he indeed in charge of all the volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. I know him personally. I met him at the command at Milan Lancuzanin's, and he was commander of all the volunteers in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he also a vojvoda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: No. He introduced himself as Major Katic at that time in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we find also another person mentioned in the next paragraph. That's Branislav Vakic from Nis who is also appointed a commander of the platoon of the volunteers from Nis and Leskovac. Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I know him through the media. I think I saw him once. Branislav Vakic, in 1992, was proclaimed a Chetnik vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we find, first of all in the quote that I just made, we find the reference to the Vukovar TO. It says here they're under the protection of the Vukovar TO. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Every volunteer unit, when it would go to the war zone, would have to report to the TO and to the command of the army of Yugoslavia. For me that is one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have in the last paragraph, we have an administrative issue that is addressed as follows: "Issue two certificates to all the soldiers, one immediately on their entry into the unit and on which the date of arrival and the notation until further notice are entered, and the second on their return on which the up to date is entered. We would like to point out that only your certificates are valid to certificate absence from place of work." Are you familiar with these certificates and why they were needed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. These certificates were issued anywhere, wherever one would go to the war operations zone. These are certificates that are then taken to the company where a person worked, and in this way one would make up for one's leave of absence. In this way, he would receive a salary. He would not have to pay his electricity bill. And then on the other hand this would certificate one's participation in the war. It would be counted as double years of service and it would be part of the retirement scheme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that -- was that similar for the regular soldiers? Did they have a similar -- similar rights. Was there any difference between the volunteers and regular soldiers in regards to these benefits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: They had the same benefits. However, volunteers, reservists of the army of Yugoslavia could become active soldiers. They could join the JNA service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is one more sentence following the previous one that I have quoted. It says here: "Please inform us in writing about the soldiers that you have sent back due to lack of discipline or any other reasons," and so forth. Was it indeed a very strict discipline among the Chetnik units? Was that actually done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such thing, of having any Chetniks returned from the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the document as such, in particular the stamp and the signature, is that an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I know the stamp. It's the stamp of the Main Committee of the Serb Radical Party in Belgrade. I also know the letterhead of the Serb Radical Party and also head of the War Staff, Ljubisa Petkovic, Vojvoda Ljubisa Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with his signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In -- in relation to Vukovar and your being there, did you ever hear complaints by a JNA officer about violent behaviour of Chetnik volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, I saw that there were conflicts between the military police and the officers of Leva Supoderica. However, the Chetniks were looting. They were caught as they were looting, and I saw them rape and kill a girl then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: On that occasion when I was at the command in Leva Supoderica in 1991, in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other crimes that Chetnik volunteers committed on the front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Not far away from that command there was a big house. They took me there. They took me to the bathroom and they boasted of having killed three Croats, that they had slaughtered three Croats, actually, and the entire bathroom had bloodstains all over. It was a horrible sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your reactions to such things that you got to know and see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, specifically that girl, I don't know her name and surname, when they brought her to the command, to Major Katic's command, in front of all of us they said they would take her so that she would show them where weapons and money were buried and that they would rape her and kill her. I reacted to that. I found this a bit strange that Major Katic and Kameni did not react to this. And when I jumped up and I said that they shouldn't touch her, then they cocked their automatic rifles and they said they would kill me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such atrocities or crimes that you saw, did you report them to -- within the Chetnik structure or the -- within -- or did you report it to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I talked to men. I talked to officer from the police. Also, the president of the Serb Radical Party in Subotica, Bozidar Vujic who is now a MP. However, they reacted to that as a completely normal thing that happened during wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Vukovar, did you see or hear about a Chetnik with the nickname Svaba.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I heard about him but I don't know who he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Specifically about Svaba, about Kinez.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the Chinaman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were Chetniks who were killing Croats in a cruel way, perhaps I should put it that. They were killing civilians in a cruel way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a particular way of killing that would indicate it was a Chetnik volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, what I saw was slit throats and noses and ears that were off cut off, massacres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware whether any of the Chetnik volunteers was disciplined, sent back from the front, prosecuted or convicted for such war crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you now actually two related documents. It's tab 10 and tab 11, and they are both actually relating to the same event. It's a public announcement by the Serbian Radical Party of north-eastern Bosnia, and it's from the commander of the Serbian Chetnik of north-eastern Bosnia, Vojvoda Blagojevic of the 27 September 1992. And they strongly protest in this document -- in this announcement against an incident that happened in September on the 24th and the 25th of September, 1992, and it says here: "That night during the curfew, special units of the MUP of Republika Srpska made up of people who are not from Semberija took away 14 members of the Zaherilic [phoen] family and eight members of the Sejmenovic family and liquidated them." And it's here actually a protest note. And looking at that second, it's actually a repetition of this protest note, and there is also a stamp. If you look at the first document, can you identify the stamps on this first document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It is the stamp of the command of the Serbian Chetniks for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was signed by Vojvoda Mirko Blagojevic. This is the old church insignia, the stamp on the first page. On the other is the stamp of the security police centre of Bijeljina, the CSB of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know this Vojvoda Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this protest note, given your own experience, what could have been the reason to make such a protest note? What could be the underlying thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I have just read through it. What it's about is that the special units of Republika Srpska, to my mind, perpetrated a crime. On the basis of the surnames I would say they were Muslim families. And the Chetniks say that it was not them who were the perpetrators but that it was the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Chetnik volunteers --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: They disassociated themselves from the crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Chetnik volunteers used as scapegoats for crimes of others? Do you know of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the help of the -- no. We have the Sanction. But I would like to put to the witness now a few -- a few documents, but they need to be in private session because a certain name appears.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to show to the witness now tab 15. It is a report on the situation on the front on the 11th and 12 December 1991. It's a report from a person I cannot identify to the War Staff of the SRS party, Ljubisa Petkovic, describing the situation at that time. Are you familiar with reports of that kind coming to -- coming in to the War Staff in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I am familiar with that, and specifically I received this report in Subotica, a photocopy of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you receive it when it is addressed to the War Staff in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: At that time, Ljubisa Petkovic would get it in the War Staff, and he would photocopy the documents and send them on to the local boards of the Serbian Radical Party in the centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To do what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, in concrete terms, this particular document is asking for assistance, reinforcements in men, fighters, to round up volunteers to send them to Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is -- this document is actually coming from the SAO Krajina, Okucani is in particular mentioned here, TO Okucani. Can Subotica actually send volunteers to Okucani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here we have as the last paragraph of this document there is the following: "We expect your help in manpower as soon and as urgently as possible and would ask the Ministry of Defence in Serbia to approve clothing, footwear, weapons, and ammunition for ..." The rest wasn't readable. "At the same time, we ask the ministry, because it is very important to fulfil the request for material and technical equipment which we sent a few days ago." Are you aware that the Ministry of Defence of Serbia was involved in those kind of matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which way they were involved? Would you know the details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, I can give you a concrete example of the officers of the army of Yugoslavia whom I've known for many years. I met them in Bosnia with all the equipment and materiel. That means they took an active part from Serbia in Croatia, Bosnia as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at tab 16. It's an order of the chief of the War Staff, Petkovic, of the 18th of November, 1991, in which he orders that all volunteers sent to Western Slavonia be put under the command of Radovan Novacic from Loznica as members of TO. Are you familiar with this person Radovan Novacic and his role in Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I've heard of him, so in that way I do know him. And he led volunteers from Serbia that were being sent to Western Slavonia. However, they were duty-bound to report to the Territorial Defence in the area of Western Slavonia once they arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where -- you have already mentioned that volunteers from Subotica were in Okucani. Do you know where else -- whether volunteers were in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, in every place and locality where there were war operations going on. So they were present everywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were SRS volunteers in Vocin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened in Vocin? Did you hear anything in relation to the treatment of Croat people in that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: As far as I remember, a massacre was committed of the civilian Croatian population in Vocin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: They were information that reached me via Belgrade or through my colleagues up at the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "via Belgrade," does it refer to the SRS party or the Chetnik movement or to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party and the command of the War Staff of the Chetnik movement as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now -- just -- I would like now to look at tab 17. It's also an authorisation from that same period of Mr. Petkovic in relation to a Milan Dobrilovic. Those two -- actually, those two authorisations that I just showed to you, are they authentic, giving the stamp and signatures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. The stamp is the same, which means the stamp of the Main Board of the Serbian Radical Party with the signature of the chief of the War Staff, Ljubisa Petkovic, and as the letterhead is the Serbian Radical Party, the War Staff, and the address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that there's been a mistake, that we're talking about two authorisations. There is actually only one authorisation, and that is issued to the name of the individual listed here who lives in Perocetkovic [phoen] number 42 street. The second name is in fact the name of a street, not the name of a person. So they're not two authorisations. It's one authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I was actually -- sorry. Yes, just to clarify, I was actually referring to the previous one. The previous one is an authorisation, and I had forgotten the witness to ask him -- forgotten to ask whether this is authentic and I just wanted to combine it. Sorry for this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document, the authorisation from the 10th of December, 1991, there is mentioned a Colonel Jovan Trbojevic. Who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: As far as I know, colonel Jovan Trbojevic was the commander of the TO in Okucani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a professional officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let us briefly look at the third authorisation. That is tab 18. It is again December 13, December 1991. Mr. Petkovic authorising again the dispatch of volunteers. And it refers now to Banja Luka. And my question to you is: Were volunteers from Bosnia actually sent to the Western Slavonia theatre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, because the Serbian Chetnik movement existed over there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the -- did there come a time when the SRS and the SCP received a request from Belgrade, SRS headquarters, to dispatch volunteers to Markusica in Eastern Slavonia to reinforce the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. An order arrived over the phone - that's how I'd put it - from the War Staff that a certain number of people were to be dispatched to Markusica to the TO, to report there, because it was the demarcation line, separation line, Markusica with the Croatian army. And we were to dispatch people to secure the line because there had been an incident there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that? Do you recall which year it was and which time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: 1992, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time from the season, giving the season. Was it in summer or winter or when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I think it was the middle of the year. Spring/summer, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we briefly go for one question into private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for your information, you can have a look at the first map where we have actually indicated this Markusica and another place that the witness is now -- will now speak about. And you can see Subotica as well and how they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you stopped in the village of Tordinci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, we were stopped. First of all in the village of Bobota by the police there, the police of Srpska Krajina, where we were told that there was fighting in and around the village of Tordinci. We entered the village of Tordinci in actual fact and we entered the war zone and stopped there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tordinci, is that a Croatian village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you came there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Once we had parked the truck on the side of the road I saw Arkan's Tigers. I saw soldiers too belonging to the Serbian Krajina, and I saw killings, the killing actually of two civilians. And in the distance some 150 -- 100 to 150 metres away, that was truck carrying dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those -- how could you identify Arkan's? Were you familiar with their outfit or how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. They wore -- actually on the right-hand side of their arms they had the Serbian Volunteer Guards insignia, and on the left-hand side they had the emblem with the Tiger on it and it said "Tigers" on the patch. They had black hoods, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having seen that, did you afterwards see any prominent politicians or perhaps Arkan himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. We arrived precisely at the time the battle was over, and there was strong fighting around the village of Lastija [phoen]. And not far from the centre I came across a television crew belonging to Radio/Television Belgrade, and Goran Hadzic and Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: I just came across them. They were congratulating each other and shaking hands, and they shook hands with me too. And later on I heard Arkan ask, "Who is this man?" But as I was wearing battle dress, he assumed he should shake hands with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much distance was between the scene where you saw Arkan's kill civilians and where Arkan and Hadzic were interviewed or filmed? Can you say how much distance there was between these two events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, I would roughly say it was between 150 to 200 metres, not more. A hundred and fifty metres let's say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they say what was going on or couldn't you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, they must have seen because the shooting was done from an automatic weapon. It was quite near. They must have turned round to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean those civilians were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. That's who I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those Arkans say something when they did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Well, before that they passed me by, two soldiers belonging to Arkan's Tigers, and they were taking away an elderly man. His hands were tied in front and there was another younger man and they were taking the two of them off. And I saw -- I heard them swearing at their -- and cursing their Ustasha Croatian mothers. And then I heard shots and saw the two of them lying down on the concrete paving dead, shot dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to show to the witness -- unfortunately, we don't have this video which was made in Markusica -- Tordinci. We couldn't get hold of this, but we have a rather similar encounter between Arkan and Hadzic, and we would like to play it. It's very brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And maybe, Witness, you can show --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: This is Arkan and Hadzic. Could you go back a little? That's Arkan on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: This one behind with the beard is Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This was taken after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's the one taken in Velepromet or somewhere like that on the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness, one question. Did you review rather -- did you review the entire tape or big parts of that tape after the fall of Vukovar, and could you see what it was, what was shown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yeah. After that, I went there and saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have actually now in the proving summary, as you can see, events in Subotica related to in a public appearance of the Chetnik unit, but as it is not crucial and time is running, I would rather drop now the chapters 29 to 31, and we may anyway come back to this during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question. The detachment in Subotica, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. It was called Jovan Nenad Crni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned in relation to this second meeting with -- with Vojislav Seselj that the village Hrtkovci was mentioned, and are you familiar with this village and who was living there in 1991/1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. I visited that village. It's a village with a majority Croatian population with a few Hungarians and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a Special Police Unit placed in that village at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. A Special Police Unit from Sremska Mitrovica was there, which was to have prevented forcible expulsions and physical attacks and harassment and even killings of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this special unit actually protect anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: As far as I know, it did not. They even assisted the leaders of the Serbian Chetnik movement at the time in moving the Croats out and escorting them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to expulsion, physical attacks, harassment and even killings, does that refer to Croats or to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- did Seselj hold a rally in Subotica in May 1992, and if so, what was the gist of his speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, did he hold a rally in Subotica and in Novi Zednik. It was like a part of the electoral campaign in those days. He was speaking and referring to Hrtkovci as an example of how things should be done, how the Hungarians and Croats should be forced to leave on their own. And if they failed to do so, then other methods should be resorted to, other coercive methods.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who received you in Bubanj Potok and dealt with you during your stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: The Chetnik volunteers was met by the officer on duty, a JNA colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bubanj Potok, is that a JNA barracks or what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: It is a military facility for training of the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An official army barracks, place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay there overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did an issue arise involving a flag, a Chetnik flag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes. The Chetnik volunteers wanted their black flag to be hoisted on the mast, but the JNA officer would not allow that. And he said the road was nearby, and a foreigner could pass by, and a Chetnik flag could not be hoisted next to the state flag, official flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you why that was not proper, why that should not be done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: First of all, this was a military facility of the army of Yugoslavia, and secondly, this was a Chetnik flag and someone might see it. A foreigner might see it. That is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive equipment and uniforms in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now go into actually several exhibits, and I think that would take another five minutes perhaps. Perhaps we could just see the -- a very brief video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's the video clip related to Seselj, and it says already on the -- on Sanction that it is May 13, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So what Seselj -- what Seselj said here on the video, is that correct? At least as far as Bubanj Potok and getting equipment there is concerned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that's a convenient time to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, it's a convenient moment. We will adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow morning. Witness C-047, would you be back then to conclude your evidence. How much longer do you think you might be in chief Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Approximately an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of June, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
